core: Sustainable innovation as socio-technical change linking technology, institutions, markets and society
Environmental and energy-system foundations, life-cycle impacts and sustainability assessment
Economics, public policy, governance, business strategy and behavioural responses in sustainability transitions
Research methods, modelling, data analysis and integrative sustainability projects
adjacent: Sustainable energy systems and the transition to renewable energy
Sustainable cities, urban planning and mobility transitions
questions: Why do sustainable technologies succeed, fail, gain acceptance or encounter resistance?
How can governments, businesses and communities design credible pathways towards low-carbon systems?

routeSelection.basis: Generic target specifies neither specialization; neither is established as universally more general. Current adopted PER Appendix2p83 lists Urban Planning and Mobility first, followed by Sustainable Energy, as does current2026cohort chart. Use neutral current order, not UCR fit. Earlier Sustainable-Energy-first basis was unsupported.

candidates.label: Sustainable energy systems and renewable transitions
Sustainable cities, urban planning and mobility
candidates.reason: Old no-available-spatial-planning reason is refuted by current workbook: ENSSUST315 is plannedSpring2028 and its description supports spatial-engineering/GIS projects. Actual EarthObservationGIS, BuildingwithNature infrastructure interventions and LivingwithWater adaptation also receive full consideration. These substantive contributions are now integrated into the closest programme. A separate duplicate urban variant is unnecessary; transport/land-use/economic urban modelling and smart-city engineering remain genuine gaps.

selection.assessment: Two related programmes pass. Closest now integrates the UrbanPlanning/Mobility interest cluster materially through spatial/geospatial/infrastructure study with economics,governance,finance,behaviour and empirical inquiry. SustainableEnergy supplies a distinct second direction. The old rejection of urban study is corrected; it is covered by the closest programme rather than manufactured as a third overlapping variant. All20eligible interests have explicit owners. Full urban/transport/energy engineering and required capstone limitations remain visible.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

alternatives.label: Sustainability transitions, urban systems & governance
alternatives.labelReason: Actual geospatial/spatial-engineering, nature-based infrastructure and water-adaptation work now joins economics,policy,governance,business,behaviour and mixed research; descriptive label does not claim full urban/mobility engineering.
alternatives.concept: Study sustainable innovation through institutions, economic incentives, public policy, business strategy and behavioural change, joined to spatial engineering, geospatial analysis, nature-based infrastructure and water adaptation. Environmental assessment and mixed research connect these strands into a related socio-technical response to the displayed Urban Planning and Mobility basis. This does not reproduce its full transport, land-use, smart-city engineering or compulsory final-project formation.
progression: Foundations in sustainability,economics,business and research precede formal dependent methods,strategic work and advanced planning/governance. Actual Spring2028 SpatialPlanning/EarthObservation/PublicEconomics and their prerequisites fit the six-term horizon. All24courses have actual offerings;7advanced courses and year1PPD. No additional hard prerequisite is inferred from course level.

alternatives.label: Renewable energy, climate & environmental systems
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres climate, renewable-system design, Earth-system tools, resources, water, environmental chemistry, circularity, remediation and quantitative analysis, supported by policy and governance.
alternatives.concept: A related sustainable-energy and environmental-systems direction supported by the programme’s available Sustainable Energy specialization: climate science, renewable-system design, resources, water, environmental chemistry, circularity, remediation and quantitative evidence. Economics, behavioural analysis, governance and environmental justice preserve socio-technical inquiry. The displayed comparator remains the neutrally selected Urban Planning and Mobility route; dedicated urban and energy engineering are not reproduced.
progression: All formal prerequisites and actual offerings verified;10advanced courses and year1PPD. ResearchDelta has no formal prerequisite and is offered only in openingFall: advisor-supported research design and investigation are its actual role, not a guaranteed engineering project. Sustainability/math/research foundations precede formal dependents. BehavioralEconomics replaces the less target-specific natural-hazards course and supplies actual behavioural experiments relevant to acceptance/incentives.
alternatives.distinctness: Each option has 9 courses (67.5 EC) absent from the other. First emphasizes spatial/geospatial/nature-based intervention, business/qualitative and civil-society/communication inquiry; second emphasizes renewable-system design, biogeochemistry/recovery, Earth resources/tools, mathematical modelling and quantitative environmental evidence.

notes.text: The UCR options provide related socio-technical sustainability programmes through actual spatial/environmental inquiry, institutions, economic incentives, business, behaviour and research, or through renewable and environmental systems. They do not reproduce TU/e’s full urban/transport engineering, land-use and smart-city design sequence, dedicated IPR/competition-law and social cost-benefit courses, or compulsory final project.

audience.programmeDescription: TU/e Sustainable Innovation studies how technological change interacts with society, institutions, markets and human behaviour. The displayed Urban Planning and Mobility specialization develops spatial and planning analysis of the built environment, transport, facilities and quality of life.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options offer related socio-technical sustainability study through actual economic, institutional, behavioural, spatial and environmental methods. The first incorporates geospatial analysis and nature-based infrastructure; the second emphasizes renewable energy and environmental systems. Both retain gaps in TU/e’s dedicated urban and transport engineering, smart-city project, specialist policy/law methods and compulsory final project.

curriculum.routeLabel: Urban Planning and Mobility specialization; ordinary 10 EC final project
curriculum.limitation: The Sustainable Energy option is a separate evidenced direction within the target programme. The displayed external curriculum remains Urban Planning and Mobility.

componentNotes.si-use-hss: Engineering Ethics and Engineering for Society each carry 5 EC. Personal and professional development is embedded. Five Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities totaling a value of seven add no credits.
componentNotes.si-multidisciplinary-cbl: Requires completion of previously offered components embedding communication, cooperation, planning and organization skills.
componentNotes.si-year2-open: 15 EC of genuine open study in year 2, followed by 30 EC in year 3. At least 30 EC of the combined 45 EC must be at intermediate or advanced level, including 15 EC at advanced level; content must not overlap. Submit a complete study plan for approval after earning 45 EC.
componentNotes.si-final-project: Required ordinary 10 EC individual research project over year-3 quarters 3 and 4. Entry requires 120 EC, including all compulsory first-year courses, Methodology for IE&IS Research, Assessment to Support Decision Making and either Sustainable Technology in Society: Advanced or Economics of Innovation: Advanced. Preparation begins in the preceding quarter. The optional Innovation Space extension is not added.
componentNotes.si-year3-open: 30 EC of genuine open study. Changes to the approved plan require approval.
